title: Rebuild only what moved
subtitle: Column-scoped change capture, a rule that chooses a full or a delta rebuild from the size of the change and never from its age, and a segment merge whose output is byte-identical to a full rebuild

stats.label: rows of embeddings the GPU files are built from
paths, delta and full, that must write the same bytes

lede: GPU workers read vectors from contiguous files on disk, built from the embedding columns of a relational database: one file of single-precision rows, one of identifiers, and for member vectors a table of offsets that maps each cluster to its range of rows. Rebuilding all of them because a few embeddings changed is a waste, and doing it on a schedule is worse, because age says nothing about whether an embedding is still correct. A trigger on each member table captures inserts and deletes, and captures an update only when the embedding column is different from its old value. Changes land in a pending table and are grouped into batches, so nothing is lost between builds.
quote: A delta build must produce exactly the file a full build would have produced, or the two paths diverge and every consumer has to care which one ran.
evidence: Change data capture in PostgreSQL: triggers that capture inserts, deletes and embedding changes into a pending table in batches, so nothing is lost between builds.
Incremental index builds: a delta rebuild that copies unchanged cluster byte ranges and rewrites only changed clusters, producing the same bytes as a full rebuild over 4 M rows.
Database-side decision logic: a SQL function choosing none, delta or full rebuild from the size of the change, full past 100,000 pending rows or 10% of the table, with no age term.
PostgreSQL performance tuning: the capture trigger's per-update function-call overhead identified, with its column-scoped fix stated as open rather than implied away.
author: Corey James
